description.en: Use the Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) to work against resistance in microgravity. Resistance training helps astronauts maintain muscle and bone strength; NASA's exercise plan schedules it separately from aerobic workouts.

fact.sourceName: NASA ISS ARED – Exercising in Space

action: An astronaut uses a resistance machine to keep muscles and bones strong.

illustration.en: An astronaut using the ARED machine.

effectText.en: The chosen astronaut goes from Tired or Stressed to Ready. The next physical mission gets a +1 bonus. Toria can also cure one crewmate's Tired condition.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Recommended: Toria or Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle; finishes before the midday phase. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: ISS data comes from microgravity. Mars gravity is about 0.38 g.

description.en: Run on the treadmill while a harness keeps your body against the belt. Treadmill and cycle-ergometer sessions help astronauts maintain cardiovascular fitness in microgravity, alongside their separate resistance-training sessions.

fact.sourceName: NASA ISS T2 Treadmill – Exercising in Space

action: An astronaut runs on a treadmill with a harness so the body stays pressed to the machine.

illustration.en: An astronaut running while strapped in.

effectText.en: Removes the Stressed condition. The chance of a negative trait is 15% lower for the rest of the day.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Recommended: Corin or Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. If Corin works alone, his Anxiety chance drops from 30% to 10% today. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: The lower negative-trait chance is a game rule.

description.en: Adjust the cabin lights to support the crew's day-night rhythm. ISS lighting research tested cooler light to support alertness and warmer light before sleep; lighting works together with scheduled sleep and other circadian cues.

action: The cabin lights change from blue-white to warm light as night comes.

illustration.en: A habitat corridor with lights that change color.

effectText.en: At night, up to two Tired astronauts can recover to Ready if they receive food and water. Avoids a Toria–Cirra fight today.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Assignment: whole habitat, no specific astronaut. Duration: 0 cycles. Valid for 1 Sol.

limitation.en: A Mars Sol lasts about 24 hours 39 minutes. The ISS sees about 16 sunrises in one orbital day.

description.en: Schedule a quiet rest period for an overworked crewmember. NASA studies show that in-flight sleep duration varies with the timing of scheduled sleep, so a planned nap can support fatigue management but does not replace adequate sleep.

action: A tired astronaut rests in a bed attached to the habitat wall.

illustration.en: An astronaut resting in a wall sleeping bag.

effectText.en: One Tired astronaut becomes Ready again and loses the extra cooldown caused by tiredness.

costText.en: Cost: no meters or rations; one astronaut cannot be assigned while resting. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: Rest time is compressed into one cycle for gameplay.

description.en: Prepare a shared meal using space-food packages and low-crumb tortillas. NASA's food-provisioning standard uses about 3,035 kcal per crewmember per day as a planning reference, while actual energy needs vary between people and missions.

action: The crew prepares a warm meal and eats together in the habitat kitchen.

illustration.en: Four astronauts eating together.

effectText.en: Removes Stressed from up to two astronauts and gives +4 Food System. Sylvan can extend the recovery to the whole crew.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3 and Food Ration −1. Recommended: Sylvan or Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: This card improves meal routine and crew mood. It does not add food mass directly.

description.en: Check each crewmember's fluid intake and replenish electrolytes when needed. NASA's human-system standard sets a minimum hydration reference of about 2.5 litres per person per day; hygiene and food preparation require additional water.

fact.sourceName: NASA ISS ECLSS – Water Recovery Milestone

action: Corin hands out drinks and records how much water each astronaut drinks.

illustration.en: Corin handing out drink pouches.

effectText.en: Life Support +5. One astronaut is protected from becoming Tired on the next mission today. Corin can protect two astronauts.

costText.en: Cost: Water Ration −1. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: One Water Ration unit is a simplification of the supply in the game.

description.en: Use low-water hygiene methods and wipe down damp surfaces while the life-support system collects cabin humidity. The ISS recovers water from humidity condensate and other sources; its approximately 98% recovery figure applies to the integrated system, not to a single wipe or dehumidifier.

fact.sourceName: NASA – Environmental Control and Life Support Systems

action: Astronauts clean up with no-rinse products while the cabin system collects moisture from the air.

illustration.en: An astronaut washing near a condensate pipe.

effectText.en: Life Support +4, one Tired astronaut becomes Ready, and +1 Water Ration is recovered at night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Recommended: any astronaut. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 1 Sol.

limitation.en: Condensate flow on Mars must be adjusted for Mars gravity, which is different from ISS microgravity.

description.en: Clean and dry the spacesuit's cooling garment and inner layers after use. NASA has studied microbial contamination and cleaning methods for suit garments, so careful hygiene is an important part of maintaining equipment shared by a crew.

action: The crew cleans and dries the cooling garment worn inside the spacesuit.

illustration.en: An astronaut drying a cooling garment.

effectText.en: Life Support +4. The risk of becoming Unwell on the next Exploration is 20% lower.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2 and Water Ration −1. Recommended: Corin or Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle. Sylvan gets +3 on his next solo Exploration. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: The 20% risk reduction is a gameplay abstraction.

description.en: Check cabin sensors and the carbon-dioxide removal system to keep the habitat atmosphere within its operating limits. ISS environmental records include cabin measurements, while the Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly uses molecular-sieve beds to remove CO2.

action: An astronaut calibrates the air sensors to make sure the scrubber system works.

illustration.en: An astronaut checking an air sensor.

effectText.en: Life Support +7. Cirra can reduce this card's Power cost to 0.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Recommended: Corin or Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: OSDR EDA comes from experiment modules in spaceflight, not from a Mars habitat.

description.en: Inspect the airlock gaskets and pressure seals before an outdoor operation. Mars has a very thin atmosphere, with surface pressure around 700 pascals at some landing sites, so a habitat must maintain a safe pressure difference between its cabin and the outside environment.

action: Toria checks the airlock gaskets and seals so they stay tight in cold Mars nights.

illustration.en: Toria scanning an airlock seal.

effectText.en: Life Support +5 and Power +3. Toria raises the Life Support recovery to +8.

costText.en: Cost: no meters, but one astronaut is locked during the task. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: Heat loss and gasket performance depend on the habitat's insulation design.

description.en: Review weather-station data before planning outdoor work. Perseverance's MEDA instrument measures Martian environmental conditions, including wind and airborne dust; atmospheric optical depth describes how much dust obscures the sky, not the electrical output of a solar panel.

action: Astronauts check the sky camera and dust sensor to learn about Mars' atmosphere.

illustration.en: An astronaut reading an optical depth chart.

effectText.en: The player learns whether a disaster will appear today and gets +4 Power.

costText.en: Cost: Power −1. Recommended: Sylvan or Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 1 Sol.

limitation.en: Solar flux measured in the atmosphere is not the same as the electricity a solar panel produces.

title.en: Brush Dust off the Solar Panels

description.en: Carry out a planned EVA to remove dust from the solar array. NASA's uncrewed InSight lander saw daily solar generation fall from roughly 5,000 to 500 watt-hours per sol as dust accumulated; manual brushing is a proposed crew-maintenance activity, not an operation performed on InSight.

action: Astronauts go outside with an anti-static brush to clean dust off the solar panels.

illustration.en: An astronaut brushing a solar panel.

effectText.en: Power +9 and the Dust-Coated Arrays penalty is removed. Cirra raises the result to +12.

costText.en: Cost: no meters. Cannot be done if Radiation Shielding is below 40 or a storm is active. Recommended: Cirra or Toria. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: InSight had no crew. Cleaning by astronauts is a game scenario and must account for EVA risk.

description.en: Inspect and clean the habitat's air-intake filters to maintain airflow and control airborne particles. NASA life-support systems manage cabin air and contaminants, but filter servicing intervals depend on the actual equipment and its maintenance procedures.

fact.sourceName: NASA – Environmental Control and Life Support Systems

action: An astronaut vacuums dust and particles from the habitat's air filter.

illustration.en: An astronaut cleaning an air filter.

effectText.en: Life Support +6 and Power +3.

costText.en: Cost: no meters, but one astronaut is locked. Recommended: any astronaut. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: Mars dust is about 1–3 µm in size and differs from the household dust particles on the ISS.

description.en: Inspect the water-recovery pumps, valves, and sensors as part of routine preventive maintenance. NASA's ISS research documents the development and operation of regenerative water systems, while specific inspection and recalibration intervals depend on the equipment.

action: Toria or Cirra checks the sensors, pumps and valves of the water recycling system.

illustration.en: An astronaut checking a water valve panel.

effectText.en: Life Support +6 and +1 Water Ration at night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Recommended: Toria or Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. If Toria and Cirra work together, the result becomes +8 Life Support, but there is still a 30% chance they fight and Radiation Shielding drops by 10. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: The +6 meter gain is a gameplay effect, not a rise in a NASA measurement.

description.en: Balance battery heating and cooling to keep the power system within its qualified temperature range. The Perseverance rover battery pack was designed for an operating range of approximately −20 °C to +30 °C; this is a mission-specific specification, not a universal limit for every battery.

action: Cirra adjusts the heaters and coolant flow of the batteries so they work in Mars nights.

illustration.en: Cirra checking a battery panel.

effectText.en: Power +8.

costText.en: Cost: Life Support −2. Cirra removes that Life Support cost. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: The extra +8 Power is an abstraction of better battery efficiency.

description.en: Check the plant pillows, moisture wicks, nutrients, and LED lighting in the crop chamber. NASA's VEG-01A red-romaine experiment used about 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ of photosynthetically active radiation and a 12:3:1 red-blue-green light ratio over a 16-hour light and 8-hour dark cycle.

action: Sylvan checks the moisture of the growing medium and the lights in the hydroponic garden.

illustration.en: Sylvan checking plants under LED lights.

effectText.en: Food System +7. Sylvan raises the result to +10.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2 and Water Ration −1. Recommended: Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: Plant care that takes weeks is compressed into one action in the simulation.

description.en: Harvest the outer lettuce leaves while leaving the plant's growing points intact. NASA's VEG-03A experiment studied repeated leaf harvest under specific growing conditions; the timing and amount of regrowth depend on the plant variety and cultivation setup.

action: Sylvan cuts the outer leaves and lets the middle of the plant grow back.

illustration.en: Sylvan cutting lettuce leaves.

effectText.en: If Food System is at least 50, gain +2 Food Ration and +3 Food System. Sylvan produces +3 Food Ration.

costText.en: Cost: no meters, but one astronaut is locked. Recommended: Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 1 Sol.

limitation.en: A single morning's harvest is compressed to fit the eight-Sol campaign.

description.en: Send recorded messages to Earth and receive replies when they arrive. The one-way light-time between Earth and Mars changes with orbital positions and is commonly about 4 to 24 minutes, so ordinary radio communication is asynchronous rather than a live conversation.

action: Astronauts swap voice messages or photos with Earth through the communication system.

illustration.en: An astronaut listening to a message at the comms console.

effectText.en: Removes Stressed from up to two astronauts and gives +3 Radiation Shielding.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. No astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles. Recommended: whole habitat. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: The Radiation Shielding boost is a game effect, not a physical effect of communication.

description.en: Set aside time for board games, music, and shared leisure. NASA analog missions schedule personal time, and astronaut journals document recreation during missions; these activities can support routine and social connection, although no fixed reduction in crew conflict is established.

fact.sourceName: NASA Human Research Program – Behavioral Health

action: All four astronauts play board games, listen to music, or do an activity together.

illustration.en: The crew playing a board game.

effectText.en: Removes Stressed from the whole crew. The Toria–Cirra fight chance drops from 30% to 10% today.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2 and Food Ration −1. No astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: The change in fight chance is a gameplay abstraction.

description.en: Write a private mission journal to record experiences, emotions, and daily challenges. NASA researchers have studied astronauts' journals to understand behavioural and psychosocial adaptation during long-duration space missions.

fact.sourceName: NASA Human Research Program – Behavioral Health

action: An astronaut writes in a journal or draws the Mars scenery to process the mission.

illustration.en: Sylvan writing in a journal by a habitat window.

effectText.en: The chosen astronaut goes from Stressed to Ready. Sylvan gives +4 Food System or +4 Radiation Shielding. Corin has no Anxiety risk when playing this card.

costText.en: Cost: no meters, but one astronaut is locked. Recommended: Sylvan or Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Valid for 2 Sols.

limitation.en: Sylvan's meter bonus is a game abstraction.

description.en: Test a water-washing process to reduce perchlorate salts in Martian soil before considering it for crops. NASA's Phoenix lander measured about 0.4–0.6% perchlorate by mass in its sampled soil; concentrations vary by location, and washing alone does not provide all the nutrients plants need.

action: Corin and Sylvan test washing perchlorate salt out of the regolith before the soil is used for plants.

illustration.en: Corin and Sylvan rinsing a sample of red soil.

effectText.en: Food System +10 and Life Support +4. Unlock: the Water cost of the Food System Upgrade drops by 1.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 and Water Ration −1. Rejection: Food System −5. Recommended: Corin and Sylvan. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises Food System to +15. Sylvan's negative group trait still applies.

limitation.en: Washed regolith still needs nutrients such as nitrogen before it can grow plants.

description.en: Tune a high-temperature solid-oxide electrolyser to extract oxygen from Mars's carbon-dioxide atmosphere. NASA's MOXIE experiment produced up to about 12 grams of oxygen per hour at a purity above 98%, demonstrating the process at small scale rather than as a crew-sized life-support plant.

action: Cirra and Corin adjust the MOXIE heater to split oxygen from Mars carbon dioxide.

illustration.en: Cirra tuning a MOXIE unit.

effectText.en: Life Support +12. Unlock: the Power cost of Life Support cards drops by 2.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6. Rejection: Life Support −5. Recommended: Corin or Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises Life Support to +18, but if he works alone he still risks Anxiety.

limitation.en: MOXIE is a demonstrator about 1% of the size needed. It is not an oxygen unit for the whole crew.

description.en: Use radiation measurements to study the Martian surface environment and model how shielding changes exposure. Curiosity's RAD instrument measured an absorbed dose rate of about 210 µGy per day during its first ten months; absorbed dose and equivalent dose are different quantities, and shielding performance depends on particle transport.

action: Corin measures how thick the regolith must be to reduce exposure to radiation particles.

illustration.en: Corin measuring a regolith sample with a dosimeter.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +12. Unlock: Radiation Shielding damage from SEP events and passive decay drops by 2.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −6. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises the result to +18.

limitation.en: Shielding performance in the game is modeled from the RAD spectrum. It is not a directly measured meter value.

title.en: Red and Blue LED Spectrum Test

description.en: Compare red, blue, and green LED combinations for growing leafy crops with controlled light. NASA's VEG-01A red-romaine study tested a 12:3:1 red-blue-green ratio at about 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; this was one experimental treatment, not a universal optimum for every crop.

action: Corin and Sylvan test LED mixes so plants get the light they need while using less power.

illustration.en: Corin and Sylvan measuring plant lights.

effectText.en: Food System +10 and Power +4. Unlock: the Power cost of night irrigation and garden lights drops from 5 to 3.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Rejection: Food System −5. Recommended: Corin or Sylvan. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises the result to +15 Food System and +6 Power.

limitation.en: The power savings over an eight-Sol campaign are a gameplay abstraction.

description.en: Study how warm, dry airflow and a membrane can recover additional water from concentrated brine. NASA's Brine Processor Assembly helped the integrated ISS water-recovery system reach about 98% overall recovery; that figure describes the whole system, not a standalone membrane.

action: The crew tests a membrane that takes water back from thick leftover liquid.

illustration.en: A technician checking a brine membrane.

effectText.en: Life Support +10 and Water Ration +2. Unlock: nightly Water Ration production increases by +1.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5. Rejection: Water Ration −2. Recommended: Corin and Toria. Duration: 2 cycles. Working together they give +15 Life Support, +3 Water Ration, and avoid Corin's Anxiety.

limitation.en: ISS membrane systems work in microgravity. Using them on Mars needs adjustment.

description.en: Test an electrodynamic dust shield that uses phased electrodes and electric fields to move dust away from a surface. NASA has studied EDS prototypes, but the technology is not yet a proven operational Mars solar-array cleaner; InSight's observed power decline was a separate mission result.

action: Cirra tests electric waves that shake Mars dust off the surface of solar panels.

illustration.en: Cirra testing a solar panel with electrodes.

effectText.en: Power +10. Unlock: Power losses from dust storms and later dust build-up are cut in half.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Corin or Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises the immediate result to +15 Power.

limitation.en: High-voltage electrodes need insulation that suits Mars' low air pressure.

description.en: Review blood and immune measurements to understand how spaceflight affects crew health. The Inspiration4 dataset includes hematology measurements from a short, approximately three-day low-Earth-orbit mission; it is research data, not proof of a universal onboard finger-prick diagnostic or illness-prevention system.

action: Corin runs blood tests to monitor the health and body response of the crew.

illustration.en: Corin reviewing blood test results.

effectText.en: Removes Tired and Stressed from the whole crew and gives +6 Life Support. Unlock: the chance of becoming Unwell drops by 20%.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Rejection: one astronaut becomes Stressed. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Corin raises Life Support to +9 and has no Anxiety when playing this card.

limitation.en: Dataset OSD-569 comes from a short low-Earth-orbit flight. The Mars health rules in the game are an abstraction.

description.en: Grow cyanobacteria in a photobioreactor as a research concept for converting carbon dioxide and light into biomass and oxygen. NASA has explored photosynthetic organisms for regenerative life support, but a Mars bioreactor that supplies crew-scale oxygen and fertilizer remains experimental.

action: Corin and Sylvan grow photosynthetic microbes in tubes to study oxygen and biomass production.

illustration.en: Green microorganism culture tubes.

effectText.en: Life Support +8 and Food System +8. Unlock: the next Food System card also gives +2 Life Support.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 and Water Ration −1. Rejection: Life Support −4 and Food System −4. Recommended: Corin and Sylvan. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises both meters to +12.

limitation.en: Closed biological systems that support a habitat are still experimental.

description.en: Analyze hydrogen-rich shielding materials using evidence from the AstroRad vest tested on Artemis I. Research reports organ- and scenario-specific dose reductions of up to roughly 60% in selected cases; this does not mean that polyethylene habitat walls provide the same level of whole-body protection.

action: Corin studies the hydrogen-rich polymer panels used in Artemis I radiation protection tests.

illustration.en: Corin checking a protective polymer panel.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +14. Unlock: astronauts cannot become Unwell from the first SEP after this technology is active.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −6. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 2 cycles. Corin raises the result to +21.

limitation.en: The data comes from the Orion mission around the Moon. Using it for Mars habitat shielding is a design adaptation.

description.en: Use ground-penetrating radar to map underground layers and investigate possible ice-bearing materials. Perseverance's RIMFAX radar operates across approximately 150–1,200 MHz and can probe more than 10 metres into the subsurface, depending on the material; radar penetration alone does not confirm an accessible ice reserve.

action: Corin and Cirra use ground-penetrating radar to map rock layers and possible ice under the habitat.

illustration.en: Corin and Cirra reading a subsurface map.

effectText.en: Power +6, Radiation Shielding +6 and Water Ration +2. Unlock: the next Exploration card can give +1 Water Ration or +3 to a meter.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6. Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Corin and Cirra. Duration: 4 cycles. Their synergy cuts the Power cost by 3, gives +9 Power and +9 Radiation Shielding, and avoids a Toria–Cirra fight because they are not both assigned.

limitation.en: The amount of ice that can be recovered from mapping is simplified for gameplay.

description.en: Excavate a selected high-latitude site to investigate shallow water ice beneath the surface. NASA orbital maps and Phoenix results support near-surface ice at some locations, but depths of only a few centimetres are local findings rather than a value that applies across Mars.

action: Sylvan digs into regolith to collect buried water ice and sends it to the purification system.

illustration.en: Sylvan holding an ice sample in a trench.

effectText.en: Water Ration +4 and Life Support +4.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Water Ration −2. Recommended: Sylvan alone. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan gets +5 Water Ration and stays Ready.

limitation.en: Shallow ice only exists in some places, mainly at latitudes above about 35°.

description.en: Collect local regolith to build a berm or fill bags around the habitat for added radiation shielding. Martian soil can provide shielding mass, but protection depends on particle energy, geometry, and secondary particles; a fixed roof thickness does not guarantee a universal dose reduction.

action: Sylvan or Toria collects regolith to add protective mass to the habitat roof.

illustration.en: An astronaut filling sandbags with regolith.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +14.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −5. Recommended: solo Sylvan or Toria. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan raises the result to +19 Radiation Shielding.

limitation.en: In a real mission, hauling heavy regolith would probably need a rover or robot.

description.en: Scout a candidate cave skylight and map the surrounding terrain before considering it for shelter. NASA images show possible cave skylights on Mars, but these openings are not confirmed accessible lava tubes or verified safe habitats for people.

fact.sourceName: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter – Planetary Caves

action: Sylvan climbs down a volcanic cave opening to check how stable and how thick the rock above is.

illustration.en: Sylvan descending into a lava tube.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +16 and Life Support +6. Unlock: the Building card BL-08 Lava Tube Sub-Bunker.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −5. Recommended: solo Sylvan. Duration: 4 cycles. Solo Sylvan gives +21 Radiation Shielding and stays Ready.

limitation.en: The stability of a cave roof must be checked before anyone lives there.

description.en: Collect layered mudstone samples and analyse them for nitrogen-bearing compounds that could support future agriculture. Curiosity detected nitrates in Martian sedimentary materials, but concentrations vary between samples and the rock would need processing before its nutrients could be used by crops.

fact.sourceName: NASA – Curiosity Finds Biologically Useful Nitrogen

action: Sylvan drills into sedimentary rock to look for nitrates that could feed plants.

illustration.en: Sylvan taking a sedimentary rock sample.

effectText.en: Food System +12 and Food Ration +1.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Food System −5. Recommended: solo Sylvan. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan gives +17 Food System and +2 Food Ration.

limitation.en: Nitrate inside rock must be processed before plants can use it as nutrients.

description.en: Track dust devils and record changes in wind and pressure near the outpost. Dust devils have been observed on Mars and can sometimes remove dust from solar-powered spacecraft, but their cleaning effect is opportunistic and cannot replace routine maintenance.

action: Sylvan or Cirra watches a dust devil and records wind changes around the solar panels.

illustration.en: An astronaut watching a dust devil.

effectText.en: Power +10 and the Dust-Coated Arrays penalty is removed.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Rejection: Power −4. Recommended: solo Sylvan or Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Solo Sylvan gives +15 Power.

limitation.en: How often dust devils happen depends on the landing site and the season.

description.en: Examine bright mineral veins for hydrated calcium sulfate, a mineral that contains chemically bound water. Opportunity observed a calcium-sulfate-rich vein at Homestake, but the rover did not demonstrate a practical process for extracting potable water from the mineral.

fact.sourceName: NASA JPL – Mars Rover Finds Mineral Vein

action: Sylvan collects gypsum rock and heats it to release the water bound inside the mineral.

illustration.en: Sylvan holding a white gypsum sample.

effectText.en: Water Ration +3 and Life Support +5.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5. Rejection: Water Ration −2. Recommended: solo Sylvan. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan makes +4 Water Ration and +10 Life Support.

limitation.en: Heating gypsum to release its water needs a lot of electrical energy.

description.en: Survey Jezero delta rocks for minerals and organic compounds using deep-ultraviolet instruments. Perseverance's SHERLOC instrument uses a 248.6 nm laser to map materials; detecting organic compounds or a potential biosignature is not proof of past or present life.

action: Sylvan collects clay from the ancient Jezero delta to study how soil holds water and signs of an old environment.

illustration.en: Sylvan scanning the delta layers.

effectText.en: Food System +8 and Radiation Shielding +8.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Rejection: Food System −4 and Radiation Shielding −4. Recommended: solo Sylvan. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan adds +5 to one meter of the player's choice.

limitation.en: Clay used for plants must be processed and sterilized first.

description.en: Evaluate a ridge-top site for solar panels by considering sunlight, orientation, wind, and dust conditions. Topography and panel tilt affect solar collection and dust accumulation; Ingenuity's solar panel recharged its batteries, but its mission does not demonstrate a ridge-mounted solar relay tower.

action: Sylvan or Cirra sets up a panel tower and repeater on a spot that gets more sunlight.

illustration.en: An astronaut setting up a solar panel tower.

effectText.en: Power +12. When finished, nightly Power recovery increases by +2 for the rest of the campaign.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: solo Sylvan or Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan gives +17 Power.

limitation.en: The tower needs insulated cable connected to the habitat.

description.en: Quarry local basaltic rock and test it as feedstock for construction materials. NASA has studied in-situ construction using local planetary materials, but strength depends on the material and processing method; basalt gravel should be tested rather than assumed to be perchlorate-free.

action: Sylvan or Toria collects basalt rock for building material and habitat shielding.

illustration.en: An astronaut collecting basalt rock.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +10 and Food System +6. The next Building card needs 4 less Power.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −5. Recommended: solo Sylvan or Toria. Duration: 2 cycles. Solo Sylvan gives +15 Radiation Shielding.

limitation.en: Sintering, or compacting, basalt takes a lot of heat energy.

description.en: Inspect shaded rocks for transient frost before sunrise and estimate whether it can be collected. Water frost has been observed at Martian landing sites, but it is thin and short-lived, and existing observations do not establish a useful water-harvesting yield.

action: Sylvan scrapes thin frost from shaded rocks before it evaporates.

illustration.en: Sylvan collecting frost from a rock.

effectText.en: Water Ration +2 and Life Support +4.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Rejection: Water Ration −1. Recommended: solo Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle. Solo Sylvan gets +3 Water Ration and +9 Life Support.

limitation.en: Natural frost is very thin. The amount of water on the card is a gameplay simplification.

description.en: Install a compact fission-power system concept to provide electricity when solar generation is low. NASA's KRUSTY experiment demonstrated a small reactor in roughly the 1-kWe class; larger 1–10 kWe systems were studied for future missions, while a 40-kWe outpost would be a proposed scale-up.

action: Toria builds a small fission reactor in a trench to supply power without relying on sunlight.

illustration.en: Toria installing a reactor with an umbrella-shaped radiator.

effectText.en: Power +18 and Life Support +4. The structure produces +5 Power every night and is not affected by dust.

costText.en: Cost: Power −8 and Radiation Shielding −4. Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 4 cycles, or 3 with Toria. Toria raises the immediate result to +23 Power. Toria and Cirra can speed it up, but have a 30% risk of conflict.

limitation.en: The reactor needs placement and shielding designed with the help of robotic systems.

description.en: Use the Sabatier reaction to combine carbon dioxide with hydrogen and produce methane and water. NASA has studied and used this chemistry in life-support systems; closing the loop for a Mars habitat would require an additional process to recover hydrogen from the methane rather than venting it.

action: Toria installs a reactor that turns carbon dioxide and hydrogen into water and methane.

illustration.en: Toria installing a Sabatier reactor tube.

effectText.en: Life Support +14 and Water Ration +2. The structure produces +1 Water Ration every night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6. Rejection: Life Support −5 and Water Ration −1. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises Life Support to +19.

limitation.en: A full system for Mars needs extra processing stages for the methane.

description.en: Use additive manufacturing to build a habitat shell from locally processed material. NASA's 3D-Printed Habitat Challenge evaluated design concepts and scaled demonstrations using simulated materials; MARSHA was an award-winning design by AI SpaceFactory, not a completed NASA-built Mars habitat.

action: Toria builds a protective layer around the habitat using local material printed into thick structures.

illustration.en: A robot printer building layers of a red dome.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +18 and Life Support +5. The structure removes the nightly passive decay of Radiation Shielding.

costText.en: Cost: Power −8. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −6. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 4 cycles, or 3 with Toria. Toria raises the result to +23 Radiation Shielding.

limitation.en: The process needs a lot of energy and sorted basalt material.

description.en: Build a vertical growing tower to use habitat space efficiently and deliver water and nutrients to plant roots. NASA Veggie experiments used plant pillows and capillary wicks, while the Advanced Plant Habitat is a separate growth chamber; this specific aeroponic tower is a proposed design.

action: Toria builds vertical plant racks that deliver a nutrient mist to the roots.

illustration.en: Toria installing a vertical plant rack.

effectText.en: Food System +15 and Food Ration +2. The structure produces +1 Food Ration every night while Food System is at least 60.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5 and Water Ration −2. Rejection: Food System −5. Recommended: Toria alone. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria gives +20 Food System. Avoid pairing Sylvan if you don't want to trigger the Power −10 risk.

limitation.en: Nightly harvests in the game are faster than real plant growth cycles.

description.en: Line a storm-shelter area with water containers and other hydrogen-rich supplies to add local radiation shielding. NASA has studied water-based materials for solar-particle-event shelters, but protection depends on the amount, placement, and energy of incoming particles and cannot block every type of space radiation.

action: Toria hangs water bags on the walls of the rest area to help reduce exposure to solar particles.

illustration.en: A sleeping area with water bags on the walls.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +16 and Life Support +4. The structure reduces SEP damage to Radiation Shielding by 8.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3 and Water Ration −2. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −6. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises the result to +21 Radiation Shielding.

limitation.en: Water used as shielding must be processed again before it is safe to drink.

description.en: Install an oxygen reserve supplied by water electrolysis and pressure storage. NASA's ISS Oxygen Generation Assembly splits water to produce oxygen; electrolysis and high-pressure storage are separate systems that require careful monitoring and fire-safety controls.

fact.sourceName: NASA – Environmental Control and Life Support Systems

action: Toria installs high-pressure oxygen storage tanks to add to the air reserve.

illustration.en: Toria securing an oxygen tank.

effectText.en: Life Support +16. The structure reduces the passive decay of Life Support by 1 every night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6 and Water Ration −1. Rejection: Life Support −5. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises the result to +21 Life Support.

limitation.en: High-pressure oxygen needs strict fire-safety procedures.

description.en: Install tilted solar panels and assess how their orientation affects sunlight, wind loading, and dust deposition. NASA studies model these trade-offs, but steep panels do not guarantee self-cleaning or a fixed increase in nightly power.

action: Toria sets up solar panels at a steeper angle so dust slides off more easily.

illustration.en: Toria installing a tilted solar panel.

effectText.en: Power +14. The structure adds +3 Power to the nightly solar recovery.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises the result to +19 Power.

limitation.en: A steeper angle can reduce how much light the panel receives at certain times.

description.en: Convert a surveyed cave entrance into a concept for a protected shelter site. Candidate cave skylights have been observed on Mars, but no accessible lava tube has been verified as a safe crew habitat and fixed radiation-protection figures have not been established.

fact.sourceName: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter – Planetary Caves

action: Toria seals and prepares a lava cave as an extra shelter.

illustration.en: A large airlock closing off a lava cave.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +22 and Life Support +8. The structure makes the crew unable to become Unwell from SEP.

costText.en: Cost: Power −8. Rejection: Radiation Shielding −5. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 4 cycles, or 3 with Toria. Toria raises the result to +27 Radiation Shielding.

limitation.en: The roof and structure of the cave must be checked before using it as a shelter.

description.en: Develop a cistern that collects, treats, and stores reusable water from habitat systems. The ISS reaches about 98% overall water recovery through its integrated life-support system, but this does not demonstrate a greenhouse-transpiration capture loop or a specific plant-water recovery rate.

action: Toria builds a tank that collects used water and water vapor from the plants.

illustration.en: Toria connecting pipes to a closed water tank.

effectText.en: Water Ration +4 and Life Support +10. The structure removes the Water Ration cost of garden irrigation every night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Rejection: Water Ration −2. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises Life Support to +15.

limitation.en: Condensate must be disinfected, for example with UV or suitable treatment, before it is used.

description.en: Install a suitport or dedicated dust-control entry area to limit Martian dust entering the pressurised habitat. NASA suitport concepts allow an astronaut to enter or leave while the suit remains outside; this differs from an air-shower mudroom and does not remove every fine dust particle by itself.

action: Toria builds a transition room that removes dust from spacesuits before the crew enters the habitat.

illustration.en: An astronaut using an EVA suit cleaning room.

effectText.en: Life Support +10 and Radiation Shielding +8. The structure removes the Tired penalty from Exploration activities.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5. Rejection: Life Support −5. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises Life Support to +15.

limitation.en: A suitport system needs a specially designed suit and connection.

description.en: Add a regenerative fuel-cell system to store surplus energy by splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen, then generate electricity when needed. NASA has studied this storage cycle, but specific energy and round-trip efficiency depend on the complete system design and are not universal flight-proven values.

fact.sourceName: NASA Glenn – Regenerative Fuel Cell Storage

action: Cirra installs hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells that can store energy for reuse.

illustration.en: Cirra connecting a fuel cell to the power system.

effectText.en: Power +16. The upgrade adds +3 Power to the nightly recovery every night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6 (−3 with Cirra) and Water Ration −1. Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. With Cirra, the gross result becomes +20 Power.

limitation.en: A round-trip efficiency of about 55% is simplified in the game calculations.

description.en: Install a smart controller that schedules electrical loads and temporarily sheds nonessential demand. Spacecraft use power-management strategies, but dimming rooms does not generate energy and no universal percentage reduction in peak demand applies to every habitat.

action: Cirra installs a computer that cuts power use in rooms that are not being used.

illustration.en: Cirra adjusting a power-use curve.

effectText.en: Power +12 and Life Support +5. All later cards need 1 less Power, minimum 0.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 (−2 with Cirra). Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. With Cirra, the gross Power result is +16.

limitation.en: This system saves energy but does not produce new energy.

description.en: Add a Brine Processor Assembly to recover additional water from concentrated urine brine. NASA's ISS system reached about 98% overall water recovery with the BPA as part of the integrated life-support system, rather than through a standalone bladder retrofit.

action: Cirra installs an extra brine processing module on the water recycling system.

illustration.en: Cirra installing a brine processing module.

effectText.en: Life Support +14 and Water Ration +3. The upgrade raises nightly Water Ration production from +3 to +4.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6 (−3 with Cirra). Rejection: Water Ration −2. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Cirra gives an extra +4 Power.

limitation.en: Hydrophobic processing bags must be replaced regularly.

description.en: Install tunable LEDs so plant-growth lighting and crew lighting can be adjusted for different needs. NASA's VEG-01A experiments measured specific red, blue, and green light treatments; they do not show that one spectrum eliminates waste heat or is best for every crop.

action: Cirra swaps the garden lights for more efficient red and blue LEDs.

illustration.en: Cirra installing LED lights over the garden.

effectText.en: Food System +14 and Power +4. The upgrade adds +1 Food Ration every night and still gives a full harvest if Food System is at least 45.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 (−2 with Cirra). Rejection: Food System −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Cirra gives an extra +8 gross Power.

limitation.en: The higher nightly harvest is sped up to fit the eight-Sol campaign.

description.en: Add an electrodynamic dust shield that uses electrodes to move charged dust away from exposed surfaces. NASA has studied EDS prototypes for planetary applications, but removal rates and long-term performance under actual Mars conditions have not yet been established.

action: Cirra installs transparent electrodes on the solar panels so dust can be shaken off with electric pulses.

illustration.en: Cirra fitting transparent electrodes onto a panel.

effectText.en: Power +12 and the Dust-Coated Arrays penalty is removed. The upgrade removes the nightly passive Power loss caused by dust.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6 (−3 with Cirra). Rejection: Power −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Cirra gives +16 gross Power.

limitation.en: The electrodes must be insulated to prevent electric sparks in Mars' low air pressure.

description.en: Evaluate hydrogen-rich polymer material as targeted radiation shielding for crew. AstroRad was tested as a wearable vest during Artemis I and showed organ- and scenario-specific benefits; those findings do not validate lining an entire habitat with the same material.

action: Cirra installs a layer of high-density polyethylene on the cabin walls and EVA gear.

illustration.en: Cirra installing polymer panels on a wall.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +16. Unlock: the safe threshold for EVA can drop from 50 to 30.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 (−2 with Cirra). Rejection: Radiation Shielding −6. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Cirra gives an extra +4 Power.

limitation.en: A vest protects certain parts of the body, not the whole habitat. GCR radiation still needs other protection such as regolith.

description.en: Use regenerative molecular-sieve beds to remove carbon dioxide from cabin air and release it during a regeneration cycle. The ISS Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly uses molecular sieves, including zeolite-based sorbents, and requires heat and a vacuum path to regenerate the beds.

fact.sourceName: NASA ECLSS – Environmental Control and Life Support

action: Cirra installs two beds of zeolite mineral that take turns catching and releasing CO₂.

illustration.en: Cirra calibrating two zeolite tubes.

effectText.en: Life Support +15. The upgrade automatically cures the Tired condition of one astronaut every night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6 (−3 with Cirra). Rejection: Life Support −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Cirra gives an extra +4 Power.

limitation.en: CO₂ regeneration and venting must be adapted to Mars' low-pressure conditions.

description.en: Add sensors and automated controls to monitor plant moisture and adjust water delivery. NASA's Advanced Plant Habitat uses extensive environmental sensors, while Veggie uses plant pillows and wicks; the proposed AI drip system and its moisture settings are habitat-design choices.

action: Cirra installs sensors and drip hoses to control root moisture precisely.

illustration.en: Cirra installing a moisture sensor on a plant.

effectText.en: Food System +14 and Food Ration +1. The upgrade adds +1 Food Ration every night if Food System is at least 60.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 (−2 with Cirra). Rejection: Food System −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Cirra gives +4 gross Power.

limitation.en: Irrigation lines still need maintenance to prevent salt build-up.

description.en: Upgrade the communications link with a high-gain Ka-band system for higher data rates when the link budget and antenna pointing allow. Ka-band operates at higher frequencies than X-band, but it requires accurate pointing and is more sensitive to atmospheric attenuation at ground stations.

action: Cirra upgrades the communication antenna so Noe can send data and warnings faster.

illustration.en: Cirra aiming a dish antenna.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +8 and Power +8. During a disaster, the player picks from four Repair cards instead of three and gets four extra mitigation options.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 (−2 with Cirra). Rejection: Radiation Shielding −4. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Cirra gives +12 gross Power.

limitation.en: Ka-band signals can be more sensitive to atmospheric conditions and dust that interfere with the signal path.

description.en: Connect equipment heat exchangers and radiators to a thermal-control loop that moves excess heat away from the habitat. The ISS uses internal water loops, external ammonia loops, heat exchangers, and radiators; a Mars system that recovers all waste heat remains a design concept.

action: Cirra connects heat from electronics to the habitat walls and tanks so heat isn't wasted.

illustration.en: Heat-exchange pipes installed in a habitat wall.

effectText.en: Power +10 and Life Support +10. The upgrade removes the passive Power decay of 3 every night.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4 (−2 with Cirra). Rejection: Life Support −5. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 2 cycles. Cirra gives an extra +14 gross Power.

limitation.en: On warmer days the system still needs radiators to get rid of extra heat.

description.en: Activate an electrodynamic dust shield to move accumulated dust from exposed surfaces during an emergency. NASA's EDS research demonstrates a possible dust-removal approach, but it has not been shown to cancel an entire Mars dust storm or achieve a fixed removal rate in storm winds.

action: Cirra turns on electric pulses from inside the habitat to shake dust off the solar panels.

illustration.en: Cirra turning on an electric cleaning panel.

effectText.en: Power +14 and cancels the Stage 3 aftermath of the dust storm.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6. Recommended: Cirra, assignment optional. Duration: 0 cycles with no crew, or 1 cycle with Cirra. Cirra gives a gross +18 Power.

limitation.en: High-voltage devices must be insulated in Mars' low-pressure atmosphere.

description.en: Send a tethered crewmember to brush dust from the solar array when conditions allow. InSight's power output declined as dust accumulated, but the lander was uncrewed; manual brushing is a proposed human-maintenance procedure that would require dust-exposure and suit-contamination controls.

action: Toria goes outside on a safety tether to clean the solar panels by hand.

illustration.en: Toria cleaning a solar panel on a safety tether.

effectText.en: Power +15 and cancels the Stage 3 aftermath. The crew who do the EVA become Tired.

costText.en: Cost: no meters. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria can give +20 Power. Toria and Cirra together can produce +24 Power, but risk a 30% conflict.

limitation.en: InSight had no crew. Manual cleaning during a storm is a game scenario and carries EVA risk.

description.en: Discharge a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell to supply emergency electricity while reactants remain. Fuel cells generate electricity and water through an electrochemical reaction, but the energy available from a complete installed system depends on reactant storage and supporting equipment.

action: The habitat turns on hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells to make electricity while dust blocks the sunlight.

illustration.en: A fuel cell feeding power to a distribution panel.

effectText.en: Power +16. The aftermath of the dust storm still applies.

costText.en: Cost: Water Ration −3. No astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles.

limitation.en: The loss of three Water Rations is an abstraction of using water reserves for the energy system.

description.en: Dim nonessential lighting and disconnect optional equipment to reduce electrical demand during a power shortage. Mars rovers have used low-power survival strategies during dust events, but a crew habitat must preserve essential heating, air circulation, and life-support functions.

action: The Commander turns off unimportant heaters, lights and fans to keep the core systems running.

illustration.en: The crew in a habitat with dim lights.

effectText.en: Power +14.

costText.en: Cost: Life Support −8. No astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles.

limitation.en: Saving power reduces the habitat's heat comfort and ventilation in the simulation.

description.en: Stow or reorient solar arrays when high winds threaten their structure. NASA studies examine the trade-off between wind loading and sunlight collection; a single wind-speed threshold or guaranteed power recovery does not apply to every array design.

action: The solar panels are tilted so less dust settles. Astronauts also record the storm conditions.

illustration.en: Solar panels stowed in a tilted position.

effectText.en: Power +10, cancels the Stage 3 aftermath, then the player picks +4 Food System or +4 Radiation Shielding.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Recommended: Cirra, assignment optional. Duration: 0 cycles with no crew, or 1 cycle with Cirra. Cirra raises the net Power recovery to +12.

limitation.en: Panels stowed upright catch less direct light.

description.en: Deploy water-filled bladders around a designated shelter area to add hydrogen-rich shielding during a solar particle event. NASA has studied water and stored supplies as local shielding, but protection depends on areal density and particle energy and does not stop all radiation.

action: Water from the supply is pumped into protective bags around the crew shelter.

illustration.en: The crew sheltering in a room with water-bag walls.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +16 and the crew is protected from becoming Unwell because of the storm.

costText.en: Cost: Water Ration −3. No astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles.

limitation.en: Three Water Rations are turned into shielding material and are not available to drink.

description.en: Place regolith-filled bags over selected habitat areas to add shielding mass. Martian soil can reduce some radiation exposure, but the effect depends on particle type, energy, thickness, and geometry; secondary particles must also be considered.

action: Toria adds regolith sandbags to the habitat roof to make the shield thicker.

illustration.en: Toria lifting regolith sandbags onto the roof.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +15. The crew who work become Tired.

costText.en: Cost: no Power or Water Ration. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises the recovery to +20 Radiation Shielding.

limitation.en: The work is done during a lull in the storm to reduce EVA exposure.

description.en: Use an AstroRad-style vest to add targeted protection to selected organs during radiation exposure. Artemis I evaluated the vest as a wearable shield, and research reports benefits for selected organs and scenarios rather than complete whole-body protection or immunity to illness.

action: Corin hands out the protective polymer vests to all astronauts.

illustration.en: Corin helping the crew put on AstroRad vests.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +12. Removes Stressed and Unwell from the whole crew and cancels the Stage 3 aftermath.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Corin raises the result to +15 Radiation Shielding and has no solo Anxiety risk.

limitation.en: The vest protects certain organs, not the whole body or the whole habitat.

description.en: Test a superconducting magnetic-field system as a research concept for deflecting charged radiation particles. NASA NIAC has funded conceptual studies, but active magnetic shielding is not a deployed Mars technology and still faces major mass, power, and field-design challenges.

action: Cirra turns on magnetic coils to form a field that can bend charged particles.

illustration.en: Cirra turning on the magnetic coils.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +16.

costText.en: Cost: Power −12, or −6 with Cirra. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Cirra gives an extra +4 Power.

limitation.en: Active magnetic shielding is still an experimental concept.

description.en: Move the crew into a compact shelter zone surrounded by water and stored supplies during a solar particle event. NASA has studied storm-shelter layouts, but this specific food-locker core arrangement and its protection value are habitat-design concepts rather than measured NASA performance.

action: The whole crew gathers in a central room surrounded by supply racks and equipment.

illustration.en: The whole crew gathered in the core room.

effectText.en: Radiation Shielding +13 and removes the Stressed condition from the crew. The whole crew is locked for 1 cycle.

costText.en: Cost: no Power or Water Ration. Assignment: whole crew automatically. Duration: 1 cycle.

limitation.en: Activity outside the habitat stops during the peak of the proton flow.

description.en: Locate a pressure leak around the airlock and apply a temporary patch while following a pressure-safety procedure. NASA guidance supports leak detection around pressure systems and seals, but this card's ultrasonic detector and universal epoxy-patch method are proposed maintenance concepts.

action: Toria looks for tiny cracks in the gasket and patches them so air doesn't leak out of the habitat.

illustration.en: Toria patching an airlock joint.

effectText.en: Life Support +15 and the Stage 3 aftermath is cancelled.

costText.en: Cost: Power −2. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises the recovery to +20 Life Support.

limitation.en: An epoxy patch needs time to cure before the airlock is used again.

description.en: Run a MOXIE-style solid-oxide system at high temperature to produce oxygen from Martian carbon dioxide. MOXIE produced up to about 12 grams of oxygen per hour at a purity above 98% in a small technology demonstration; a crew-scale system would require major development.

action: Cirra runs MOXIE at high temperature to make oxygen from Mars carbon dioxide.

illustration.en: Cirra turning on a MOXIE unit.

effectText.en: Life Support +16 and one Tired astronaut becomes Ready again.

costText.en: Cost: Power −12, or −6 with Cirra. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Cirra gives an extra +4 Power.

limitation.en: A human base needs an oxygen system far larger than the MOXIE demonstrator.

description.en: Regenerate a saturated molecular-sieve bed by heating it and exposing it to a vacuum path so captured carbon dioxide can be released. NASA's ISS Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly uses this approach, but the exact temperature depends on the system design.

action: The system heats the zeolite tubes to release the trapped carbon dioxide and restart the scrubber.

illustration.en: Zeolite tubes giving off steam as they heat.

effectText.en: Life Support +12 and removes the Tired condition from two affected astronauts.

costText.en: Cost: Power −6. No astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles.

limitation.en: Heating for regeneration needs extra electricity.

description.en: Activate a single-use solid chlorate oxygen generator as a backup oxygen source. NASA has studied solid chlorate candles for emergency oxygen delivery; the chemical reaction releases heat and requires careful handling, so the system is not risk-free or reusable.

fact.sourceName: NASA ECLSS – Environmental Control and Life Support

action: Corin activates a chemical canister that releases oxygen without using electricity.

illustration.en: Corin watching an oxygen-generating canister.

effectText.en: Life Support +14.

costText.en: Cost: Food System −3. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Corin has no Anxiety risk when playing this card alone.

limitation.en: The device is single-use and gives off heat while it works.

description.en: Use a greenhouse crop chamber as a small experimental part of a biological life-support loop. Plants absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis, but a small Veggie crop chamber cannot replace engineered cabin CO2 removal or supply oxygen at crew scale.

action: Sylvan opens the air ducts to the garden so the plants help absorb some of the cabin CO₂.

illustration.en: Sylvan opening a vent to the garden.

effectText.en: Life Support +15 and one Tired astronaut becomes Ready again.

costText.en: Cost: Food System −6, or −3 with Sylvan. Recommended: Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle. Sylvan reduces the Food System impact to −3.

limitation.en: A small garden only absorbs a small part of the CO₂ the whole crew makes.

description.en: Repair the brine-processing water system and check for deposits that can interfere with fluid flow. NASA has documented calcium-sulfate precipitation in urine-processing equipment, but routine pump rebuilding in the manner shown is not established as a standard crew procedure.

action: Toria repairs the pumps and valves of the water processing system so water flows normally again.

illustration.en: Toria replacing a valve on a water pump.

effectText.en: Food System +14 and Water Ration +2.

costText.en: Cost: Power −3. Recommended: Toria. Duration: 2 cycles, or 1 with Toria. Toria raises Food System to +19 and still gives +2 Water Ration.

limitation.en: Fixing ISS equipment in real conditions needs special procedures and handling tools.

description.en: Restore water delivery through the capillary wicks in the plant pillows. NASA Veggie experiments use wicks to carry water to seeds and roots, but crop survival time and emergency repair performance depend on the specific hardware and growing conditions.

action: Sylvan connects capillary tubes straight to the growing medium so the roots get water again.

illustration.en: Sylvan connecting a capillary pipe to the growing medium.

effectText.en: Food System +16 and the Stage 3 aftermath is cancelled, so the harvest can run tonight.

costText.en: Cost: Power −5. Recommended: Sylvan. Duration: 1 cycle. Sylvan raises the result to +19 Food System.

limitation.en: A capillary system works best for certain plants, including leafy vegetables.

description.en: Investigate scale buildup in the urine-processing line and restore flow using a tested maintenance method. NASA reports describe calcium-sulfate precipitation and process or chemical approaches to control it; ultrasonic scale clearing is a fictional repair technology in this game.

fact.sourceName: NASA ECLSS – Environmental Control and Life Support

action: Cirra sends ultrasonic waves to loosen mineral scale that blocks the water lines.

illustration.en: Cirra fitting an ultrasonic transducer onto a pipe.

effectText.en: Food System +14 and Water Ration +1.

costText.en: Cost: Power −10, or −5 with Cirra. Recommended: Cirra. Duration: 1 cycle. Cirra gives +4 Power.

limitation.en: Ultrasonic cleaning on the card is a mechanical adaptation for gameplay.

title.en: Distill Waste Water for Medical Use

description.en: Process recovered greywater through multiple treatment stages before it is considered reusable. ISS water recovery includes distillation, filtration, catalytic treatment, and water-quality monitoring; boiling and condensing water alone does not guarantee potable quality.

action: Corin distills used water through heating and condensation to make water that can be reused.

illustration.en: Corin operating a distillation device.

effectText.en: Water Ration +3 and Food System +8.

costText.en: Cost: Power −4. Recommended: Corin. Duration: 1 cycle. Corin raises Food System to +12 and has no solo Anxiety risk.

limitation.en: Batch distillation needs a lot of energy for every liter of water.

description.en: Restore nutrient delivery to the crop pillows and flush the root zone with an appropriate water-and-nutrient mix. NASA Veggie pillows used controlled-release fertilizer, but the specific 18-6-8 formulation and emergency nutrient-gel recipe are not established by the cited study.

action: The crew mixes N-P-K nutrient gel and gives it straight to the growing medium.

illustration.en: An astronaut pouring nutrient gel into a root container.

effectText.en: Food System +15.

costText.en: Cost: Food Ration −2. No Power or astronaut needed. Duration: 0 cycles.

limitation.en: Two Food Rations are traded for a Food System boost as a gameplay abstraction.
